author: H. K. Moody
title: Angie Craig highlights energy relief act and ACA anniversary in latest statements
text:
U.S. Representative Angie Craig, who has served Minnesota’s 2nd district since 2019, addressed several issues on her official Twitter account on March 23, 2026.
In a post from that day, Craig highlighted the financial pressures Minnesotans are facing regarding utility costs and announced new legislation: “Minnesotans are facing higher-than-ever electricity bills and skyrocketing gas prices, and large corporations are forcing consumers to foot the bill. I’m proud to introduce the Energy Bills Relief Act, which will expand Minnesotans’ access to affordable, clean energy and make” (March 23, 2026).
Later the same day, she marked the anniversary of a significant healthcare milestone while criticizing political opponents: “16 years ago today, President Obama signed the Affordable Care Act into law — bringing health care coverage to millions of Americans. Today, Trump and Republicans are hell bent on gutting the ACA — but we can’t let them. I won’t stop fighting to ensure Minnesotans have access to” (March 23, 2026).
In another post on March 23, Craig celebrated a sports achievement: “This is a historic and well-deserved win not only for today’s women athletes but for generations to come. Congratulations to the players on this hard fought victory. As the players’ union said, now it’s time to get back to the game…Let’s go Lynx!”
Craig has represented Minnesota’s 2nd District in Congress since replacing Jason Lewis in 2019. She was born in West Helena, Arkansas in 1972 and currently resides in Prior Lake. Craig earned her BA from the University of Memphis in 1994.
